newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Yen, Swiss franc in focus on Hungary FX futures mkt.
newsitem.headline: Yen, Swiss franc in focus on Hungary FX futures mkt.

text.p: Plummeting yen futures were in focus on the Budapest Commodity Exchange (BCE) on Friday, traders said.
"Yen prices experienced a relatively strong correction mainly due to lower spot prices," said Imre Uzonyi of Swap.

Yen futures dropped for all contracts, with the fall diminishing towards the longest maturities. June dropped 95 fillers to 148.05, September went down 1.30 forints to 155.80 but March 1988 only lost 70 fillers to finish at 167.40.
September was the most popular maturity, with 9,030 yen contracts, 5,900 for German marks and 4,100 for the Swiss franc.
"September is the favourite maturity for speculation at the moment as the large number of open contracts and the relatively distant maturity date leave plenty of space for manoeuvering," Uzonyi said.
Tradeless Italian lira futures rose for two maturities, going up 1.60 forints for September to end at 112.50 and closing at 115 forints for December, up 1.55.
Total BCE trade was a below-average 3.8 billion forints, or 25,801 contracts, with yens accounting for 11,400 lots, Swiss franc for 7,491 and marks for 4,300.
Budapest Stock Exchange's currency futures market was tradeless for the fifth day.
